title: A grantee's board member gave $25,000 to the Mayor's own measure committee

beats.text: In San Francisco,

steps.name: Her committees

beats.text: a contractor’s board members can’t give money to the official who approved its contract.

steps.name: Her committees

beats.text: Not for 12 months.

steps.name: Her committees
steps.sub: no gifts from GLIDE’s board for 12 months

beats.text: So here’s the case. A GLIDE board member gave to a committee that named the Mayor as its controller. How much?

visual.label: One gift
visual.sub: to a committee naming the Mayor as controlling officeholder

beats.text: 25,000 dollars.

visual.label: from the GLIDE board member, Jan 25, 2024

beats.text: This is a lead, not a finding.

visual.line: This is a lead, not a finding: a pattern in public records. This film says what the records show, what they do not show, and what would settle it.

beats.text: First, what’s on the record.

visual.label: Free Meals grant
visual.sub: second amendment, approved by the Mayor Mar 10, 2023

beats.text: In March 2023,

visual.label: Free Meals grant
visual.sub: second amendment, approved by the Mayor Mar 10, 2023

beats.text: Mayor Breed approved more money for GLIDE’s Free Meals grant:

visual.label: Free Meals grant
visual.sub: second amendment, approved by the Mayor Mar 10, 2023

beats.text: 4,187,149 dollars.

visual.label: Free Meals grant
visual.sub: second amendment, approved by the Mayor Mar 10, 2023

beats.text: That raised the grant’s limit to 12,055,383 dollars.
The Mayor’s own form lists the donor on GLIDE’s board.

visual.line: lists the donor by name on GLIDE's board

beats.text: The committee that got the gift backed Prop E, a police measure.

visual.label: Yes on Prop E
visual.sub: marked Controlled, signed by London Breed

beats.text: Its 2025 amended filing is marked controlled by the Mayor. And she signed it.

visual.label: Yes on Prop E
visual.sub: marked Controlled, signed by London Breed

beats.text: Its own Form 410 named her as controlling officeholder from January 10,

visual.line: Form 410, amended Jan 10, 2024: controlled committee, London Breed, Mayor, controlling officeholder

beats.text: 2024: 15 days before the gift.

visual.line: Form 410, amended Jan 10, 2024: controlled committee, London Breed, Mayor, controlling officeholder

beats.text: The first lead is the timing. The grant was approved. Then the gift came. How many days later?
321 days.

visual.label: days after the Mayor’s approval
visual.sub: 331 after the Board’s vote; inside the 12-month ban

beats.text: That’s inside the 12 months. GLIDE’s tax returns list her on its board through June 2025.

visual.line: a board member in each year from July 2022 to June 2025

beats.text: The second lead is a late form. It names who is barred from giving.
It’s due in five business days. How late was it?
65 days after the Board’s vote. 55 after the Mayor’s approval.
So for two months, no public record showed that GLIDE’s board was covered.

visual.line: for two months there was no public record that GLIDE’s board members were covered

beats.text: That’s typical.

visual.label: of 3,830 Mayor’s notices since 2019 filed after the deadline

beats.text: 2,497 of the Mayor’s 3,830 notices since 2019 came in late.

visual.label: of 3,830 Mayor’s notices since 2019 filed after the deadline

beats.text: The third lead: was the money sent back? If the rule applied, the committee shouldn’t keep it.
We searched its filings. No payment back to the donor. Nothing handed over to the City.
The refunds on file are vendors paying money back to the committee, plus two payments received in error.

visual.line: the only refunds are vendor refunds to the committee, and the only reversals are of two payments received in error

beats.text: None of that money involves the donor.

visual.line: the only refunds are vendor refunds to the committee, and the only reversals are of two payments received in error

beats.text: The fourth lead is enforcement.
The Ethics Commission’s last penalty under this rule was in October 2021: 750 dollars.
Five years without a case. So matches like this one aren’t being tested in public.
The records don’t show the exact dates of her board service.

cards: The exact dates of her board service

beats.text: Or that any rule was broken. Or any link between the gift and the grant.

cards: Any link between the gift and the grant

beats.text: What would settle it? GLIDE’s board lists with dates.

cards.what: The committee’s original filings and any review

beats.text: And the committee’s first filings, and any review.

cards.what: The committee’s original filings and any review

beats.text: No refund, forfeiture or enforcement action is on record. No authority has ruled on it.
A lead is a question, not an accusation.
